evidence.claim: George Bennett gave Bandon the name of his County Cork hometown and introduced gorse to the area.
evidence.quote: The community was named by George Bennett, an Irish immigrant who settled in the area in 1873 and named the town after his hometown of Bandon, County Cork in Ireland.

evidence.claim: The spiny plant spread through the town and countryside.
evidence.quote: George Bennett also introduced gorse (Ulex europaeus) into the local area, which in the following decades went wild and became a nuisance in both the town and in the neighboring countryside.

evidence.claim: In September 1936, a forest fire swept into Bandon and destroyed its entire commercial district.
evidence.quote: On September 26, 1936, a fire burned several miles of forest east of town. But a sudden shift in the wind drove the flames swiftly westward.

evidence.claim: Before the fire, part of that district stood on wooden pilings over the Coquille River, with river traffic reaching merchants’ doors.
evidence.quote: Part of the commercial district had been erected on wooden pilings jutting out over the Coquille River not far from the South Jetty, accommodating river traffic at the merchants' doors.

evidence.claim: Rebuilding kept the business district within the available land.
evidence.quote: After the 1936 fire, when Bandon began to be rebuilt, the new perimeter of the business district did not extend beyond the available land.

flags: ODOT calls this a Tour Route and gives 41 miles including the cape excursion and retrace; material’s mapped line is 25 miles. Used the official itinerary and label.
No road construction or designation history is cached; park acquisition history supplies the documented historical narrative.
ODOT gives three miles from Sunset Bay to Shore Acres; the park articles give about one mile. Exact interpark distance omitted.
Simpson’s middle initial differs: B. in ODOT, J. in the park article. Omitted the initial.

The Bandon article gives both 1885 and 1855 for cranberry introduction and places McFarlin’s first bog near Hauser. Dropped the current precise 1885 origin narrative because the cache is internally inconsistent.

The current swimmer-warmth claim is in ODOT but omitted rather than presented as a swimming guarantee. Ghost-forest age and earthquake origin have only secondary cache support; no tide or exposure conditions are supplied.
